summary:
The biggest story right now is the FDA's order (Nov 9–10) to add a warning to every GLP-1 label about NAION, a rare cause of sudden vision loss. Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy are all named. Mainstream news has covered it heavily (AP, CNN, CBS, BBC, WSJ, NPR, STAT), but almost nobody on YouTube has made a calm, practical "will tirzepatide hurt my eyes, and what should I watch for" video yet. That's our best opening.

Fresh research this week:
- **T-REx (Nature Medicine, Nov 9):** randomized trial in 120 adults aged 50–70 without diabetes, 40 weeks. Tirzepatide plus resistance training 3 times a week lost about 25% less lean tissue than tirzepatide alone, with the same ~22 kg weight loss. Strength rose about 10% with training and fell about 10% without.
- **ATTAIN-OSA (AHA, Nov 10):** orforglipron cut sleep apnea events by about 18 an hour vs about 5 on placebo, in 712 adults without diabetes.
- **TRIUMPH-4 (ACR, Nov 8):** full retatrutide knee osteoarthritis data.
- **Italian records study (Lancet Regional Health–Europe):** about 80,000 adults with type 2 diabetes. Stopping a GLP-1 was linked to about twice the rate of heart attack, stroke or death. It's observational, and the authors say it can't show cause and effect.

Seasonal timing: Thanksgiving is building toward its Nov 18–27 peak, and alcohol and heartburn questions come with it.

Two things to know before you plan with this:
- The dehydration/sick-day and diarrhoea long videos shipped Nov 7–10, so I've left them off the list.
- I couldn't find a confirmed full REDEFINE 4 session at ObesityWeek. Topline results came out in February 2026, so a 13:00 Short qualifies only if new data actually appear Nov 14–17.

Gray-market and compounded signals are rejected: the compounded price report, the Philippines "research use" tirzepatide warning, and the Hims sales angle.

candidates.topic: FDA orders NAION (rare sudden vision loss) warning on all GLP-1 labels, including tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) and semaglutide (Nov 9–10, 2026)
candidates.angle: Calm 'worried → answered' explainer: what NAION is (reduced blood flow to the front of the optic nerve, usually sudden and painless), why the FDA added it to Warnings and Precautions, how rare it is (EMA PRAC: may affect up to 1 in 10,000 people on semaglutide for at least a year), why the evidence is mixed and the companies say cause hasn't been established, and the one action that matters: sudden vision loss or blurred or missing parts of vision means urgent care. Name both NANOS and the AAO. Don't-stop line scoped to emergencies. Long-form framed as a practical, evergreen body question ('Tirzepatide and Your Eyes: What to Watch For'), not as news.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–5 days for news searches; 'tirzepatide vision' searches stay high for weeks as patients see the updated label
candidates.why_now: The FDA required label changes across about a dozen GLP-1s on Nov 9–10, with saturated coverage from AP, CNN, CBS, BBC, WSJ, NPR, STAT, Healthline and Fierce. Viewers on tirzepatide will search 'is my vision safe?' as the new labels and pharmacy leaflets reach them. Creator coverage leans on scary 'blindness' headlines, so a calm, label-accurate version stands out.

evidence.signal: FDA orders the NAION risk added to about a dozen GLP-1 labels, including Ozempic and Zepbound
FDA requires a Warnings and Precautions update for Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy
'FDA's GLP-1 vision warning rests on mixed evidence', useful for calibrating the wording
Nov 2 review of GLP-1 ocular safety and retinal outcomes

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus resistance training: T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, Nov 9). About 25% less lean-tissue loss, and strength up about 10% vs down about 10%
candidates.angle: 'Will tirzepatide shrink my muscles?' answered with a fresh randomized result. 120 adults aged 50–70 with overweight or obesity and no type 2 diabetes, 40 weeks, both groups on tirzepatide. The group doing resistance training 3 times a week lost the same ~22 kg and ~17 kg of fat, but about 25% less lean tissue, and their strength rose about 10% while the tirzepatide-only group's fell about 10%. Results are averages. Pair it with Medscape's 'GLP-1 muscle loss claim: what's true'. Use it as the 13:00 Short and as a fresh-hook pinned comment on Strength. No new long-form, because single-trial deep dives are banned and the topic overlaps Strength.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Published Nov 9 in Nature Medicine, with UWA and Medical Xpress releases on Nov 10 and a Medscape myth-check the same day. Health-creator coverage hasn't started, and muscle loss is a proven worry for our audience.

evidence.signal: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy: randomized controlled trial
T-REx: 120 adults, 40 weeks, 25% less lean loss, strength +10% vs −10%
'The GLP-1 Muscle Loss Claim: What's True, What's Not' (Nov 10)

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 regain data, refreshed by the Italian records study linking GLP-1 discontinuation to higher heart risk in type 2 diabetes (Lancet Reg Health Eur, Nov 10)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form next to our best-CTR video (Stopping). 'Thinking about stopping? What the research says helps.' Cover SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88; placebo still 9.9% below starting weight on average), then the habits linked to keeping results (protein, strength training, follow-up plans), and the reminder that stopping is a decision to make with your prescriber. The Italian study is a hook only: about 80,000 adults with type 2 diabetes and no heart disease, about 4 vs 2 events per 100 people a year. It's observational, so 'linked to', and the authors say stopping may not be the cause. No fear framing and no 'never stop' message.
keywords: what happens when you stop Zepbound
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress ('Stopping Ozempic may be bad for your health') and The Independent ('little-known risk of stopping weight-loss injections') both ran Nov 10. Our own Stopping video has an 8.84% CTR. The New Year 'should I stop?' cycle is close.

evidence.signal: Italian records study: ~80,000 adults with type 2 diabetes; about 2× combined heart attack, stroke or death with discontinuation; observational
Mainstream pickup: 'little-known risk of stopping weight-loss injections'

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, eating slower, smaller plates and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Shorts pointing to the live Thanksgiving long-form, each answering one fresh question: 'Will I feel sick after a big meal on tirzepatide?', 'Why do I feel full after 5 bites?', 'Is it OK to skip dessert at the table?' Calm, no extreme-diet messaging.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 10 straight snapshots with rising momentum. The seasonal search peak is 1–2 weeks out, and we already have the long-form to funnel into.

evidence.signal: Seen 10 times, momentum rising from 84 to 93
'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects' (Nov 10): mainstream interest in GI effects

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol at holiday parties: what the label says, plus the new semaglutide/tirzepatide alcohol-outcomes target trial emulation (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know'. Why some people say drinks feel different (the reward-system research), how alcohol and a full stomach add to nausea and dehydration, and the low-blood-sugar caveat for people also on insulin or sulfonylureas. Never give a 'safe amount'. The new study is observational, in type 2 diabetes only, so 'linked to'. The semaglutide addiction trial news (The Pharmacist, Nov 10) is 'being tested', not proven.
candidates.why_now: The holiday party season starts now, and new observational data plus a new semaglutide addiction trial are in the news. The playbook names it as a priority Lane A topic.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide, tirzepatide and recorded alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes: target trial emulation
Systematic review of incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder
Semaglutide to be tested for alcohol and opioid addiction (Nov 10)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: redness, itching and small lumps. What the label reports (6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg, vs about 2% on placebo) and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: Normal?' A calm walkthrough of what's common, what's in the label, practical pen-day tips (rotating sites, letting the pen reach room temperature as the IFU says), and when it isn't normal: signs of a serious allergic reaction, which are post-marketing reports, mean stop and get medical help right away. Line 1 Watch next link from Side Effects.
candidates.why_now: It's playbook priority #1 for new Lane A, and its Short reached 232 views (top quartile). Seen in 8 snapshots. Searches rise as new starters begin before the New Year.

evidence.signal: Injection-site Short 232 views; seen in 8 snapshots

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why slower gastric emptying causes sulfur burps and reflux after big meals, and what helps
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide Burping and Heartburn: What Helps', timed for heavy holiday meals. The mechanism (food stays in the stomach longer), label rates for eructation (burping) and GERD in both arms, practical habits (smaller portions, not lying down soon after eating, slower eating), and when symptoms that won't settle mean calling the prescriber. Check with a pharmacist before reaching for an antacid alongside other medicines.
candidates.why_now: Holiday meals amplify reflux. It's a playbook Lane A priority, and no live video of ours answers it.

evidence.signal: 'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects' (Nov 10)

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) cuts sleep apnea severity: ATTAIN-OSA phase 3, AHA Scientific Sessions, Nov 10
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short with a fresh randomized result: two double-blind trials in 712 adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea, BMI 27 or above and no diabetes (one with CPAP users, one without). Breathing interruptions fell by about 18 events an hour on orforglipron vs about 5 on placebo. Then connect it to tirzepatide's existing sleep-apnea approval (separate trials, not head-to-head). Preliminary conference data, not yet peer-reviewed.
candidates.why_now: Presented Nov 10 at AHA, with a Lilly press release and Medical Xpress and Time coverage. Orforglipron is the only non-Lane-A topic that earns search for us, and creator coverage is thin.

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-OSA: 712 adults; about −18 vs −5 events an hour; AHA late-breaker
Foundayo significantly reduced OSA severity

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: full TRIUMPH-4 phase 3 data at ACR 2026 (Nov 8)
candidates.angle: 13:00 'What's confirmed?' Short. In adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis, retatrutide reduced the WOMAC pain score by up to an average of 4.5 points at 68 weeks vs placebo (from Lilly's topline). Say clearly that it isn't approved anywhere, and that online 'research' products aren't the trial drug (MHRA warning, AJMC on gray-market retatrutide). Average change in pain score, compared with placebo.
candidates.why_now: Presented at ACR Nov 8, with coverage from Medscape, MedPage, Everyday Health, Time and Newsmax. Retatrutide 'new phase 3 data' Shorts are a proven format (126–280 views).

evidence.signal: Retatrutide improves knee OA pain and physical function (Nov 9)
TRIUMPH-4 topline: WOMAC pain −4.5 points (75.8%) at 68 weeks
How plans and clinicians should handle gray-market retatrutide (Nov 10)

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): REDEFINE 4, CagriSema vs tirzepatide in adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks)
candidates.angle: Tirzepatide-first head-to-head Short ('Tirzepatide vs CagriSema: What the Head-to-Head Found'): 809 adults with obesity. Average weight loss was 23.0% with CagriSema vs 25.5% with tirzepatide 15 mg if everyone stayed on treatment (20.2% vs 23.6% counting everyone who started), so non-inferiority was not met. Topline came out Feb 2026, so don't call it new. Make the Short only if new full data appear at ObesityWeek. If new randomized data go public, it could qualify as the extra L2.
candidates.why_now: The conference is 4 days out, and tirzepatide-first head-to-heads in obesity get 108–176 views on our Shorts. I couldn't confirm a REDEFINE 4 session at ObesityWeek, so watch the program.

evidence.signal: REDEFINE 4: 23.0% vs 25.5%, non-inferiority not met (Feb 2026)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the thyroid warning: what's confirmed? New Endocrine Reviews review of preclinical and human data on GLP-1 medicines and thyroid cancer (Nov 6)
candidates.angle: Body-worry Short ('Will tirzepatide affect my thyroid?'). The boxed warning comes from rodent C-cell tumours. The new review weighs the human data, which are mixed and mostly observational. Cover who the label says shouldn't use it (personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2) and which neck symptoms to report. With the eye warning in the news, 'what other warnings are on my label?' is a natural follow-on question.
candidates.why_now: It's a fresh major review, seen in 3 snapshots, and the label-warning conversation has just been reopened by the NAION order.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 receptor agonists and thyroid cancer: review of preclinical and human data

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and gout: new systematic review and meta-analysis on serum uric acid, hyperuricemia and gout (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 8)
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight Short: what the pooled data show for uric acid and gout flares, with the class-level scope ('GLP-1 medicines', not tirzepatide-specific unless the paper breaks it out). Check the abstract for tirzepatide data before titling. Holiday rich-food season gives it a hook.
candidates.why_now: Published Nov 8 with no press pickup yet. Gout is common in our audience, and holiday food is a seasonal trigger.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs on hyperuricemia, serum uric acid and gout: systematic review and meta-analysis

candidates.topic: Painkillers while on a GLP-1 during cold season: NSAID initiation and GI bleeding risk in GLP-1 users (Am J Health Syst Pharm, Nov 5)
candidates.angle: 'Is it OK to take ibuprofen on tirzepatide?' Keep it observational ('linked to'), name the population and comparator, and send people to their pharmacist or prescriber before new pain or cold medicines. Fits a sick-day series but needs careful fact-checking. Observational angles underperform as Shorts, so treat it as a future long-form section rather than a standalone piece.
keywords: can I take Advil on Mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Fresh retrospective cohort, it's cold season, and no creator coverage yet.

evidence.source: PubMed / Am J Health Syst Pharm
evidence.signal: NSAID initiation and GI bleeding risk in GLP-1 RA users: retrospective cohort

candidates.topic: Pregnancy planning on GLP-1s: 'Ozempic baby boom' (NPR) plus an Adelaide sheep study suggesting semaglutide may lower fetal oxygen (Nov 10)
candidates.angle: Only as a calm 'what the label says' Short: GLP-1 medicines aren't recommended in pregnancy, the label advises stopping ahead of a planned pregnancy (follow the label's exact wording and timing), and the tirzepatide oral-contraceptive note applies. The sheep study is an animal result and must be called one. Point to the Birth Control long-form.
candidates.why_now: NPR, Medical Xpress, Earth.com and Brighter Side all ran pregnancy stories Nov 9–10. It's a strong curiosity topic, but it's easy to turn into fear bait.

evidence.signal: 'An Ozempic baby boom? The GLP-1 pregnancy plot twist' (Nov 9)
Semaglutide may lower fetal oxygen levels, sheep study suggests

candidates.topic: ER visits for GLP-1 side effects rising (WBAL, Nov 10), with poison-centre calls tied to dosing mix-ups
candidates.angle: Only as a reassurance piece: which side effects mean urgent care (severe stomach pain that won't settle, signs of dehydration, sudden vision loss, allergic reaction) and which usually settle. Never discuss dosing, and never mention compounded sources. Use it as a section inside the side-effect long-forms, not as a standalone news piece.
keywords: when to go to ER on tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Local TV pickup on the same day as the FDA eye warning, which adds to a 'side-effect anxiety' news cycle.

evidence.signal: 'ERs see surge in GLP-1 side effects | What to know' (Nov 10)

candidates.topic: REJECT: compounded tirzepatide price report (Ozari Health, $125–$199 a month), 'Tirzepatide 30 mg research use' vials (Philippines FDA advisory), Apothecary Pharma compounded vial recall, and Lilly–Hims sales angles
candidates.angle: Don't cover these. They promote or normalise compounded, gray-market or research-chemical sources, and cost or pharmacy topics are banned. At most, the 1-per-week gray-market Short can say generically that 'research use' products aren't the approved medicine, with no prices, providers or links.
candidates.why_now: These are high-volume commercial signals that breach the never-cover list.

evidence.signal: Compounded tirzepatide price report
